question: Should OpenClaw adopt this deny-over-allow exec policy as a long-term operator contract in both openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json, including its inherited plugin SDK exposure?
rationale: Source review and live proof can establish correctness, but they cannot choose permanent security semantics, parallel persisted policy ownership, or which helpers become supported external API.

options.title: Accept a narrowed contract
options.body: Retain the proven enforcement behavior, confirm whether both persisted layers are necessary, and prevent incidental plugin SDK exports unless plugins need them.

options.title: Accept the current contract
options.body: Own both persisted configuration layers and the inherited SDK surface as long-term compatibility commitments.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open until maintainers choose a smaller or different exec-policy model.

recommendation.title: Accept a narrowed contract
recommendation.body: Retain the proven enforcement behavior, confirm whether both persisted layers are necessary, and prevent incidental plugin SDK exports unless plugins need them.

likelyOwner.reason: The dominant history across the central exec approval and host-policy files makes this the best available security-contract decision owner.
